shorts.title: What you will learn: Searching
shorts.hook: Find one item among a million in about twenty steps.
shorts.script: Find one item among a million in about twenty steps. Today we search. One method is simple. The other is clever, and it finds one item among a million in about twenty steps. Linear search checks the items one by one, from the start. It works on any data, but it can be slow. Binary search needs sorted data. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Searching.

shorts.title: Searching in one minute
shorts.hook: Linear search checks the items one by one, from the start.
shorts.script: Linear search checks the items one by one, from the start. It works on any data, but it can be slow. Binary search needs sorted data. It looks at the middle item, and then it throws away half of the range. Think of a dictionary. You open it in the middle, then you pick the left or the right half. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Searching in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: Low and high mark the part of the array that is still possible.
shorts.script: Low and high mark the part of the array that is still possible. Mid is the middle index. If the middle item is the target, we are done. If it is too small, we move low past mid. If it is too big, we move high below mid. When low passes high, the target is not there. The program prints two. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: Binary search on unsorted data
shorts.script: Bug of the Day. The array holds three, but the search says minus one. The array is not sorted. Binary search looks at nine in the middle. Nine is bigger than three, so it throws away the right half. But the three was in the right half. Sort the array first. Binary search throws away half of the range using the order of the items. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: BINARY SEARCH ON UNSORTED DATA
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: Binary search on unsorted data.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: I use binary search to find my socks. Half of the drawer is always wrong.
shorts.script: I use binary search to find my socks. Half of the drawer is always wrong. Write a linear search that finds a name in an array of five strings. Print the index, or minus one. Write your answer in the comments. Linear search checks the items one by one. Binary search halves the range each time. Binary search needs sorted data. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pun and challenge.
